question: I have only Basic Autoplan and caused a crash in B.C. What coverage distinction matters before I assume my own car's repairs will be paid?
generated_answer:
A very important question! In British Columbia, if you have only Basic Autoplan coverage and are involved in a crash, the distinction that matters is whether you are considered "at-fault" or "not at-fault" for the accident.

**At-Fault:**
If you are deemed at-fault for the crash, your Basic Autoplan coverage will only cover the damages to the other vehicle(s) or property involved, up to the policy limits. However, your own vehicle's repairs will not be covered by ICBC (Insurance Corporation of British Columbia), unless you have purchased additional coverage, such as Collision coverage.

**Not At-Fault:**
If you are not at-fault for the crash, the other driver's insurance (also provided by ICBC, if they are a B.C. resident) should cover the damages to your vehicle. In this case, you can make a claim against the other driver's insurance, and their policy should pay for your vehicle's repairs.

To determine fault, ICBC will investigate the accident and assign a percentage of fault to each driver involved, based on the circumstances of the crash. If you are found to be partially at-fault (e.g., 50% or more), you may still be responsible for paying for your own vehicle's repairs, unless you have additional coverage.

It's essential to report the accident to ICBC and provide detailed information about the crash, including any witness statements, photos, or other evidence. This will help ICBC determine fault and process your claim accordingly.

Keep in mind that even if you are not at-fault, you may still need to pay a deductible if you have Collision coverage or other additional coverage. It's always a good idea to review your policy and understand what is covered and what is not, to avoid any surprises in the event of a claim.
